key_insight: A fine-tuned LLM could extract diagnostic gross brain findings from autopsy narratives and help classify major neurodegenerative diseases with good overall performance, especially for PSP and MSA.
clinical_relevance: This suggests routine autopsy gross descriptions may be a useful source of structured diagnostic information, but mixed pathologies like AD-LBD remain hard to separate.
method: 5,613 Mayo Clinic Brain Bank autopsy cases (1998–2023) across 7 neuropathologic diagnoses.
LLM extracted 39 gross brain features from narrative autopsy reports; CatBoost and a second text-based LLM used these features plus age, sex, and brain weight.
Performance was tested on a held-out set of 562 cases.
evidence_signal: In held-out testing, CatBoost reached 0.73 accuracy and 0.92 macro-AUC, while the text-based LLM reached 0.75 accuracy; extraction accuracy was 0.95 on 200 annotated feature-level examples.
watch_item: Results come from a single brain bank and autopsy setting, so performance may not generalize to other centers, and combined AD-LBD remained difficult to identify accurately.
paper_title: Diagnostic Value of Large Language Model-Extracted Gross Brain Findings in Neurodegenerative Diseases
